drawings.name: line_tired_dog_street
drawings.prompt: A very tired shaggy dog lies flat on the pavement at the edge of a wide empty street, right next to a zebra crossing, chin on its front paws, eyes half closed, ears drooping, one big yawn, a few small curly lines above its head to show sleepiness. The zebra crossing stripes run away across the wide street towards the far pavement, which is far away. The kerb and the crossing are seen slightly from above. Nothing else: no cars, no people, no signs, no buildings. Landscape image 1536x1024; the dog in the left half, large; the dog and the street together fill about 90% of the width and about 70% of the height. No text, no letters, no numbers, no road markings other than the plain zebra stripes.

drawings.name: line_word_three_things
drawings.prompt: One invented friendly character (simple round face, dot eyes, short messy hair, a plain sweater) stands facing us, full figure, and carries three things at once: the right hand holds a blank paper card high above the head, like asking a question at an auction; a large blank round name badge is pinned on the chest; the left arm hugs a small closed cardboard parcel tied with string against the hip. The three things are big, clear and well separated so each can be labelled later. Portrait image 1024x1536; the character fills about 75% of the width and about 85% of the height, centred. The card, badge and parcel are blank: no text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols.

drawings.name: line_three_readers
drawings.prompt: Three invented students (simple round faces, dot eyes; one with glasses, one with a ponytail, one with a cap) stand side by side in front of one long blank paper banner pinned flat on a wall at their eye level. Each student holds up a big round magnifying glass, and the three glasses point at three different spots on the same banner: the left student looks at the left end, the middle student at the middle, the right student near the right end. They look focused and calm. Landscape image 1536x1024; the banner runs across about 90% of the width in the upper half; the students fill about 85% of the width and about 80% of the height. The banner is blank paper: no text, no letters, no lines of writing, no numbers.
